title: Separate post on OL-DL 1-on-1's: • The tackles showed Arvell Reese it's not going to be easy to line up on the edge and win at this level. Reese used his bend to get the edge on Andrew Thomas, but Thomas recovered and pushed Reese wide of the QB. Reese tried to rush inside on Jermaine Eluemunor and Eluemunor held him off. Josh Ezeudu had a good rep stuffing an outside rush from Reese. In a 2-on-2 rep with Thomas and Jon Runyan against Reese and Chauncey Golston, Thomas stoned Reese. Thomas is ridiculously good in 1-on-1s, which are slanted toward the pass rushers. Abdul Carter tried to beat Thomas inside with a spin, but Thomas pushed him into the ground. • Kayvon Thibodeaux continues to develop his inside rush moves. He beat Francis Mauigoa on his outside shoulder on a rep. Mauigoa held his ground on a bull rush from Darius Alexander. Thibodeaux got a pressure inside while running a stunt with Carter against the right side of the OL. JC Davis did a good job pushing Thibodeaux wide in a rep at tackle. • Jon Michael Schmitz had two solid reps against Alexander and DJ Reader. Thought Shelby Harris shed Jon Runyan for a win, while Runyan held up against a bull rush from Golston.

title: Apologies for the delayed practice report, but the WV sun is sneaky intense and wiped me out today. Anyway, here's what stood out: • This is the first time the Giants didn't practice "good on good" with the first-team offense facing off against the first-team defense. Harbaugh said in those instances, both coordinators are calling their side of the ball like it's a game. When he mixes the 1's against the 2's like today, the coordinator for the first-team unit can request looks from the other side so they can work against specific coverages, pressures, etc. • Harbaugh was excited about Jaxson Dart's practice. It got off to a rocky start with a pair of interceptions. Safety Raheem Layne had a pick on a throw to Darnell Mooney over the middle. It was a little high and tipped off of Mooney's hands and Layne grabbed it. Safety Elijah Campbell intercepted a deep out intended for Calvin Austin. Dart seemed a tad late to pull the trigger and Campbell did a good job closing on the ball. We saw some more of Dart holding the ball and scrambling, but that's not always on him. There were a lot of third-and-long situations today and there wasn't always an open receiver. Dart had some good throws on intermediate routes. The highlight was a deep out to Odell Beckham Jr. while rolling right. The 1's squared off in the low red zone to end practice. Dart hit Theo Johnson for a touchdown on the last play after rolling right and then scrambling back to his left. • The biggest difference between Dart and Jameis Winston is how decisive Winston is. That shows up in the red zone when timing is paramount. Winston was firing bullets against the first-team defense in a red zone drill. On three straight plays he fired TDs to JuJu Smith-Schuster, Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson. JuJu was back after missing yesterday's practice with knee swelling and he delivered an impressive grab over Tyler Nubin for the TD. There's always a flip side with Winston, who floated a bad interception to CB Art Green in a red-zone period to end practice. • This was easily the best practice of Odell's comeback. He caught two passes from Dart and one apiece from Winston and Brandon Allen. Odell showed his burst after catching a crosser from Dart and turning up the sideline. He also showed he still has elite body control by getting his feet inbounds on the deep out from Dart. • Nubin has had a quiet camp (not necessarily bad for a safety). He was heavily involved today. He combined with Kayvon Thibodeaux (running with the 1's in place of Brian Burns) for a sack in a red-zone period and then did a good job bodying up Theo Johnson in the back of the end zone to break-up a pass. He gave up a TD to JuJu on a similar play. • Cam Skattebo had a noticeably lighter workload. That's going to need to happen for players as they make their way through this grueling camp. Skattebo broke a long run early in practice, lowering his shoulder into Campbell downfield before Layne punched the ball out and Korie Black recovered. • Deonte Banks got more work with the 1's and Paulson Adebo got more time with the 2's 👀 • The highlight of the 9-on-7 period is watching Patrick Ricard lead block. Abdul Carter did a good job today of delivering a hit to Ricard to set the edge. • The Giants practiced the victory formation. Details. • Dominic Zvada went 10-for-10 on field goals. Believe the long was 54. He's 28-for-31 in camp. Making a strong push for the kicker job. • Not surprisingly, Harbaugh intently watches special teams period. He got involved and coached up the gunners at one point.

• This is the first time the Giants didn't practice "good on good" with the first-team offense facing off against the first-team defense. Harbaugh said in those instances, both coordinators are calling their side of the ball like it's a game. When he mixes the 1's against the 2's like today, the coordinator for the first-team unit can request looks from the other side so they can work against specific coverages, pressures, etc.

• Harbaugh was excited about Jaxson Dart's practice. It got off to a rocky start with a pair of interceptions. Safety Raheem Layne had a pick on a throw to Darnell Mooney over the middle. It was a little high and tipped off of Mooney's hands and Layne grabbed it.

Safety Elijah Campbell intercepted a deep out intended for Calvin Austin. Dart seemed a tad late to pull the trigger and Campbell did a good job closing on the ball.

We saw some more of Dart holding the ball and scrambling, but that's not always on him. There were a lot of third-and-long situations today and there wasn't always an open receiver. 

Dart had some good throws on intermediate routes. The highlight was a deep out to Odell Beckham Jr. while rolling right. 

The 1's squared off in the low red zone to end practice. Dart hit Theo Johnson for a touchdown on the last play after rolling right and then scrambling back to his left. 

• The biggest difference between Dart and Jameis Winston is how decisive Winston is. That shows up in the red zone when timing is paramount. Winston was firing bullets against the first-team defense in a red zone drill. On three straight plays he fired TDs to JuJu Smith-Schuster, Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson. JuJu was back after missing yesterday's practice with knee swelling and he delivered an impressive grab over Tyler Nubin for the TD. 

There's always a flip side with Winston, who floated a bad interception to CB Art Green in a red-zone period to end practice. 

• This was easily the best practice of Odell's comeback. He caught two passes from Dart and one apiece from Winston and Brandon Allen. Odell showed his burst after catching a crosser from Dart and turning up the sideline. He also showed he still has elite body control by getting his feet inbounds on the deep out from Dart. 

• Nubin has had a quiet camp (not necessarily bad for a safety). He was heavily involved today. He combined with Kayvon Thibodeaux (running with the 1's in place of Brian Burns) for a sack in a red-zone period and then did a good job bodying up Theo Johnson in the back of the end zone to break-up a pass. He gave up a TD to JuJu on a similar play. 

• Cam Skattebo had a noticeably lighter workload. That's going to need to happen for players as they make their way through this grueling camp. Skattebo broke a long run early in practice, lowering his shoulder into Campbell downfield before Layne punched the ball out and Korie Black recovered. 

• Deonte Banks got more work with the 1's and Paulson Adebo got more time with the 2's 👀

• The highlight of the 9-on-7 period is watching Patrick Ricard lead block. Abdul Carter did a good job today of delivering a hit to Ricard to set the edge. 

• The Giants practiced the victory formation. Details. 

• Dominic Zvada went 10-for-10 on field goals. Believe the long was 54. He's 28-for-31 in camp. Making a strong push for the kicker job. 

• Not surprisingly, Harbaugh intently watches special teams period. He got involved and coached up the gunners at one point.
full_text:
Apologies for the delayed practice report, but the WV sun is sneaky intense and wiped me out today. Anyway, here's what stood out:

• This is the first time the Giants didn't practice "good on good" with the first-team offense facing off against the first-team defense. Harbaugh said in those instances, both coordinators are calling their side of the ball like it's a game. When he mixes the 1's against the 2's like today, the coordinator for the first-team unit can request looks from the other side so they can work against specific coverages, pressures, etc.

• Harbaugh was excited about Jaxson Dart's practice. It got off to a rocky start with a pair of interceptions. Safety Raheem Layne had a pick on a throw to Darnell Mooney over the middle. It was a little high and tipped off of Mooney's hands and Layne grabbed it.

Safety Elijah Campbell intercepted a deep out intended for Calvin Austin. Dart seemed a tad late to pull the trigger and Campbell did a good job closing on the ball.

We saw some more of Dart holding the ball and scrambling, but that's not always on him. There were a lot of third-and-long situations today and there wasn't always an open receiver. 

Dart had some good throws on intermediate routes. The highlight was a deep out to Odell Beckham Jr. while rolling right. 

The 1's squared off in the low red zone to end practice. Dart hit Theo Johnson for a touchdown on the last play after rolling right and then scrambling back to his left. 

• The biggest difference between Dart and Jameis Winston is how decisive Winston is. That shows up in the red zone when timing is paramount. Winston was firing bullets against the first-team defense in a red zone drill. On three straight plays he fired TDs to JuJu Smith-Schuster, Jalin Hyatt and Xavier Gipson. JuJu was back after missing yesterday's practice with knee swelling and he delivered an impressive grab over Tyler Nubin for the TD. 

There's always a flip side with Winston, who floated a bad interception to CB Art Green in a red-zone period to end practice. 

• This was easily the best practice of Odell's comeback. He caught two passes from Dart and one apiece from Winston and Brandon Allen. Odell showed his burst after catching a crosser from Dart and turning up the sideline. He also showed he still has elite body control by getting his feet inbounds on the deep out from Dart. 

• Nubin has had a quiet camp (not necessarily bad for a safety). He was heavily involved today. He combined with Kayvon Thibodeaux (running with the 1's in place of Brian Burns) for a sack in a red-zone period and then did a good job bodying up Theo Johnson in the back of the end zone to break-up a pass. He gave up a TD to JuJu on a similar play. 

• Cam Skattebo had a noticeably lighter workload. That's going to need to happen for players as they make their way through this grueling camp. Skattebo broke a long run early in practice, lowering his shoulder into Campbell downfield before Layne punched the ball out and Korie Black recovered. 

• Deonte Banks got more work with the 1's and Paulson Adebo got more time with the 2's 👀

• The highlight of the 9-on-7 period is watching Patrick Ricard lead block. Abdul Carter did a good job today of delivering a hit to Ricard to set the edge.

title: Why are the Commanders signing Stefon Diggs? Many reasons, obviously, but one could be the large amount of checkdowns we've been seeing in training camp so far. In the 2025 regular season, on first downs, Diggs caught: 31 of 33 targets for 400 yards, at 12.9 yards per reception. With zero drops. This opens the door for David Blough to use early-down play-action, stay ahead of the chains, and get Jayden Daniels easy completions without making the offense overly reliant on checkdowns by using Diggs behind linebackers or in displaced coverage.

I think the big thing that showed up was penalties. So we’ve made a big emphasis of how we place our hands, how we’ve gotta finish with our feet. “We want to be better in the penalty aspect of it. I think that’s gonna have a huge impact on our return game. We had some big returns that got called back. Those ended up being huge yard losses. It goes back to those fundamentals.”

title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 7: - By the end of Wednesday's practice, the Niners had 20 players (including the 3 on PUP) not participating because of injury. In 2024, they had 23 not practicing when they canceled joint practices with the Saints. Chris Foerster says that's not something that's come up to him with the Titans for next week, though it could have been discussed elsewhere in the building. Don't think the Niners are super concerned that the injuries they have (aside from Pearsall) are long term but they still need to have enough healthy bodies to handle the rigors of joint practices. - The full list of those missing practice today: New additions: DE Nick Bosa (soreness), LB Dre Greenlaw (soreness), DT Osa Odighizuwa (soreness), OL Carver Willis (concussion), WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (undisclosed). Shaken up in practice: OL Nick Zakelj, DE Sam Okuayinonu Previously disclosed: WR Christian Kirk (calf), WR Mike Evans (quad), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle) PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) - For the record, many of these guys, including Evans and Kirk did some work on the side, including some full speed running. Guerendo and Mustapha, in particular seem to be close to back. Greenlaw also seemed to be fine as he got a bit of a rest today with soreness. He watched practice from the defensive back field. - Coach Kyle Shanahan continues to be out around his normal time (10:47 today for those keeping score) and handling more and more. Not quite fully back but still seems to be trending the right way. - The Niners released DT Kevin Givens and DL Cam Sample and signed DL Ogbo Okoronkwo and WR KhaDarel Hodge. - Niners had enough OL and DL to do some one-on-ones today... Halton's fresh legs showed up here a few times, including a really strong rush against Zakelj and a solid one against Robert Jones. His quickness and burst is evident. Just a matter of staying healthy and getting much needed reps... Okoronkwo also has some fresh legs and had a nice power rush against Enrique Cruz Jr., who has struggled in this drill... Good day for Sebastian Valdez both in one on ones and in team. He gave Connor Colby some problems here then had success in team... Austen Pleasants took a rep or two at right guard here which is unusual. Foerster indicated he wanted to move a handful of OL around in these drills but the injuries messed up those plans. Presumably, Pleasants got to move because of that... CJ West showed his power a few times, including against Jones and Zakelj, though Jake Brendel had a good rep against him... Romello Height is made for this drill in some ways. His first step and bend impresses nearly every time. Will need to expand his bag (and maybe it's already there) a bit but the tools to be effective in obvious passing situations seem apparent. He had a good rep against Colton McKivitz who has otherwise been stout in these. - Speaking of the offensive line, Jones got his first crack at running at left guard with the 1s today with Colby getting reps with the 2s and 3s. Foerster said he hoped to get Colby some work on the right side and had all kinds of plans to move the pieces around a bit but injuries to Toth and Willis scuttled that. Not sure this means a big change in the plans but worth noting and following. - DT Alfred Collins got his first extended work in team periods after returning from PUP last week. Haven't seen Collins in 1v1 yet but a step forward for him, especially with Odighizuwa not participating today. - With Greenlaw watching, Garret Wallow got a look at the weak side linebacker spot. Also, Nick Martin was supposedly shaken up last open practice but he was on the field today seemingly no worse for the wear. - A really good practice for QB Brock Purdy despite musical pass catchers. Had him at 13-of-14 (he had another one broken up by Lenoir but looked like a would-be sack first) on the day and the one incompletion could have been a flag as LB Garret Wallow either perfectly timed or was a bit early on a throw to RB Christian McCaffrey. Some highlights from Purdy: Escaped pressure from Height, rolled to his right, got a good block from TE Luke Farrell and dropped one in the bucket to McCaffrey over the middle for a big gain... In a three-play red zone sequence, he threw a TD to Patrick Taylor Jr. on a ball that was perfectly placed low and to the left where only Taylor could get it as Ji'Ayir Brown closed in from the other side then ran for a score on a designed run and finished by rolling out and finding Junior Bergen for a touchdown. He capped practice finding WR Jordan Watkins deep down the left side for another score in move the ball. - Farrell hasn't proved much of an option in the pass game since his arrival but he was very involved on Wednesday. Had him down for five catches, all from Purdy, including three in the move the ball period to set up Watkins' TD. Jake Tonges has been more involved, too, and with all the injuries at WR, it's clear Purdy has a level of comfort with the TEs that can pay dividends. - Watkins is putting together a nice camp and Purdy has faith in him but he also has had some go through his hands that he probably should have had. A good opportunity right now for him to carve out a role given all the other injuries. The good outweighs the bad, just needs a bit more consistency. - Foerster said McCaffrey and LT Trent Williams are on a rep count in this camp, as you'd expect. But he also tipped his hat to them for being at practice every day and setting a tone for the young players. Both were their usual, productive selves on Wednesday. - Best defensive play of the day came when CB Jack Jones jumped in front of a pass from Martinez to deflect it into the waiting arms of LB Jaden Dugger. Dugger caught it and returned it for a would-be pick-6. - Among the other defensive highlights from team drills: Okuayinonu got some pressure and a would-be sack but if it wasn't, Lenoir had yet another PBU. Darrell Luter Jr. had a nice pass breakup on a throw to the end zone for Demarcus Robinson from Martinez. West burst through for a run stuff on the first play of team. LB Fred Warner snuffed out a run for McCaffrey early in that period, also. Halton stuffed Khalil Herbert with a quick move in the first period for the 3s. A nice PBU on a throw for TE Brayden Willis, was hard to tell but I *think* it was Siran Neal who knocked it away. LB Jalen Graham also had a nice read and run stuff against Sincere McCormick. CB Ephesians Prysock with sticky coverage to deny a deep ball from Kurtis Rourke for Wesley Grimes. - The Niners are back at it tomorrow after AC/DC plays Levi's tonight. In the year 2026, I wouldn't think they still move the needle enough to have concerts at a place as big as Levi's but here they are. Can only respect it for a group that's been doing it for more than five decades. Shoutout to them. Thanks for reading.

Greenlaw also seemed to be fine as he got a bit of a rest today with soreness. He watched practice from the defensive back field. 

- Coach Kyle Shanahan continues to be out around his normal time (10:47 today for those keeping score) and handling more and more. Not quite fully back but still seems to be trending the right way. 

- The Niners released DT Kevin Givens and DL Cam Sample and signed DL Ogbo Okoronkwo and WR KhaDarel Hodge. 

- Niners had enough OL and DL to do some one-on-ones today... Halton's fresh legs showed up here a few times, including a really strong rush against Zakelj and a solid one against Robert Jones. His quickness and burst is evident. Just a matter of staying healthy and getting much needed reps... Okoronkwo also has some fresh legs and had a nice power rush against Enrique Cruz Jr., who has struggled in this drill... Good day for Sebastian Valdez both in one on ones and in team. He gave Connor Colby some problems here then had success in team... Austen Pleasants took a rep or two at right guard here which is unusual. Foerster indicated he wanted to move a handful of OL around in these drills but the injuries messed up those plans. Presumably, Pleasants got to move because of that... CJ West showed his power a few times, including against Jones and Zakelj, though Jake Brendel had a good rep against him... Romello Height is made for this drill in some ways. His first step and bend impresses nearly every time. Will need to expand his bag (and maybe it's already there) a bit but the tools to be effective in obvious passing situations seem apparent. He had a good rep against Colton McKivitz who has otherwise been stout in these.

- Speaking of the offensive line, Jones got his first crack at running at left guard with the 1s today with Colby getting reps with the 2s and 3s. Foerster said he hoped to get Colby some work on the right side and had all kinds of plans to move the pieces around a bit but injuries to Toth and Willis scuttled that. Not sure this means a big change in the plans but worth noting and following. 

- DT Alfred Collins got his first extended work in team periods after returning from PUP last week. Haven't seen Collins in 1v1 yet but a step forward for him, especially with Odighizuwa not participating today. 

- With Greenlaw watching, Garret Wallow got a look at the weak side linebacker spot. Also, Nick Martin was supposedly shaken up last open practice but he was on the field today seemingly no worse for the wear. 

- A really good practice for QB Brock Purdy despite musical pass catchers. Had him at 13-of-14 (he had another one broken up by Lenoir but looked like a would-be sack first) on the day and the one incompletion could have been a flag as LB Garret Wallow either perfectly timed or was a bit early on a throw to RB Christian McCaffrey. Some highlights from Purdy: Escaped pressure from Height, rolled to his right, got a good block from TE Luke Farrell and dropped one in the bucket to McCaffrey over the middle for a big gain... In a three-play red zone sequence, he threw a TD to Patrick Taylor Jr. on a ball that was perfectly placed low and to the left where only Taylor could get it as Ji'Ayir Brown closed in from the other side then ran for a score on a designed run and finished by rolling out and finding Junior Bergen for a touchdown. He capped practice finding WR Jordan Watkins deep down the left side for another score in move the ball. 

- Farrell hasn't proved much of an option in the pass game since his arrival but he was very involved on Wednesday. Had him down for five catches, all from Purdy, including three in the move the ball period to set up Watkins' TD. Jake Tonges has been more involved, too, and with all the injuries at WR, it's clear Purdy has a level of comfort with the TEs that can pay dividends. 

- Watkins is putting together a nice camp and Purdy has faith in him but he also has had some go through his hands that he probably should have had. A good opportunity right now for him to carve out a role given all the other injuries. The good outweighs the bad, just needs a bit more consistency. 

- Foerster said McCaffrey and LT Trent Williams are on a rep count in this camp, as you'd expect. But he also tipped his hat to them for being at practice every day and setting a tone for the young players. Both were their usual, productive selves on Wednesday. 

- Best defensive play of the day came when CB Jack Jones jumped in front of a pass from Martinez to deflect it into the waiting arms of LB Jaden Dugger. Dugger caught it and returned it for a would-be pick-6. 

- Among the other defensive highlights from team drills: Okuayinonu got some pressure and a would-be sack but if it wasn't, Lenoir had yet another PBU. Darrell Luter Jr. had a nice pass breakup on a throw to the end zone for Demarcus Robinson from Martinez. West burst through for a run stuff on the first play of team. LB Fred Warner snuffed out a run for McCaffrey early in that period, also. Halton stuffed Khalil Herbert with a quick move in the first period for the 3s. A nice PBU on a throw for TE Brayden Willis, was hard to tell but I *think* it was Siran Neal who knocked it away. LB Jalen Graham also had a nice read and run stuff against Sincere McCormick. CB Ephesians Prysock with sticky coverage to deny a deep ball from Kurtis Rourke for Wesley Grimes. 

- The Niners are back at it tomorrow after AC/DC plays Levi's tonight.  In the year 2026, I wouldn't think they still move the needle enough to have concerts at a place as big as Levi's but here they are. Can only respect it for a group that's been doing it for more than five decades. Shoutout to them. Thanks for reading.

title: Some highlights from 49ers practice Wednesday... 🏈Jaden Dugger, back at LB after a day with the DE, notched a pick 6 off a Jack Jones tip (Adrian Martinez was QB). Hybrid defender development in full force! 🏈LG is far from settled. Vet Robert Jones was with the first teamers instead of Connor Colby. There's been no lights-out option in 1-on-1s. Chris Foerster wants to mix and match the interior line during practice to prep for in-season challenges. So we should see some creativity when Carver Willis and Brett Toth return 🏈TE Luke Farrell is much more involved in the pass game than last season. Caught 3 more passes from Brock Purdy today, including one in a tight window off a sidearm delivery 🏈Explosive win for rookie DT Gracen Halton, making his return from a bone bruise, in 1-on-1s over Nick Zakelj. Halton was very fired up 🏈Purdy did the Dougie after a red-zone TD run. He also hit CMC downfield off a rollout on a sweet play design. Great camp for CMC continues 🏈Purdy hit Jordan Watkins for a big gainer to end practice. Watkins also caught a TD from Mac Jones 🏈Deebo can still move. Stretched the field effectively on a sweep today. Incentive watch this season will be fun 🏈Demarcus Robinson fought back to make a physical catch over the middle vs Ashtyn Davis. Luter, Darrell Luter Jr. won a red-zone rep vs Robinson for a nice PBU 🏈49ers were down about 20 players by end of practice, but many absences are precautionary 🏈Dre Greenlaw (soreness, but healthy) watched practice from centerfield next to Lynch and Shanahan. Looked like he was taking mental reps with each snap 🏈Alfred Collins and CJ West are big dudes

title: Vic Fangio on Jordan Davis as a pass rusher: "It first started towards the end of the '24 season. He got in better shape. He's a much better pass rusher in the 330s than what he was. Wicks had the catch of the day on Wednesday when he came down with a Hurts throw along the left sideline. Wicks had two defenders around him but was able to concentrate and hold onto the ball despite so much traffic around him. Wicks has now strung together three-straight practices where he has been the best receiver on the field and probably has the two most impressive catches of camp overall, starting with his catch over two defenders this past Saturday on a deep pass. Wicks has 15 targets in six training camp practices, which is the most on the team. His nine catches is third most of the 26 players who have at least one target. No player’s stock is rising more at the moment than Wicks
